prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the StreamableHTTP client exhausts its SSE reconnection attempts after a server disconnect, the failure is currently swallowed silently (only a debug log), leaving the in-flight request's caller hanging forever with no response or exception. Both PRs target exactly this 'reconnection failure' path in `_handle_reconnection`/its callers, just via different signaling mechanisms: #2395 constructs a `JSONRPCError` and sends it through `ctx.read_stream_writer` so the specific pending request resolves with an error (skipping notifications via an `isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest)` guard), while #3098 instead raises a `StreamableHTTPError`, adding an `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull it out of anyio's `ExceptionGroup` wrapping so it propagates to the caller as a Python exception. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395's fix is per-request: it targets the specific pending JSON-RPC call via read_stream_writer and explicitly checks `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which expect no reply) aren't mishandled, plus it upgrades the log line from debug to warning for better observability of exhausted retries. #3098's diff includes an unrelated revert of `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` back to `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of the file, which is a stale-branch/rebase artifact and a likely source of merge conflicts against current main; its exception-based approach also surfaces failure at the connection/exception-group level rather than resolving the specific in-flight request that was waiting.

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py where WWW-Authenticate header parameter matching was based on naive substring/regex checks, which could incorrectly match on partial parameter names or mis-split values containing commas inside quoted strings. Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer to replace the old approach. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py where WWW-Authenticate header parameter matching was based on naive substring/regex checks, which could incorrectly match on partial parameter names or mis-split values containing commas inside quoted strings. Both add a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer to replace the old approach. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add near-identical quote/escape-aware comma splitters (compare the char-by-char loops in _iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041 - same logic, same edge cases handled for backslash escapes inside quotes). The functional difference: #3012's _iter_www_auth_params finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which assumes the header contains a single challenge/scheme. #3041 goes further with _extract_bearer_auth_params, which partitions each top-level segment into scheme/remainder and explicitly scopes extraction to segments belonging to the 'Bearer' scheme, so it degrades correctly instead of merging params from a second scheme (e.g. a trailing DPoP challenge) into the Bearer result. This makes #3041 the more complete fix for headers with multiple concatenated challenges.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly attempts JSON-parsing string values for parameters typed as a union including str (e.g. str | None), corrupting valid strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. '{"a":1}' passed as a plain str). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py incorrectly attempts JSON-parsing string values for parameters typed as a union including str (e.g. str | None), corrupting valid strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. '{"a":1}' passed as a plain str). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() before checking the union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP pattern Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None. 2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` directly against the raw union args without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated-wrapped str member (very common when params carry a Field description) is not recognized as 'simple' and pre_parse_json would still attempt to JSON-decode it, leaving the corruption bug unfixed for that common case. 2032 does cover a broader set of unions (str|int, str|float, str|bool) that 3056 doesn't address, but it misses the Annotated case that's central to the reported bug.

clusters.pick_reason: 3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() before checking the union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP pattern Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None. 2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` directly against the raw union args without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated-wrapped str member (very common when params carry a Field description) is not recognized as 'simple' and pre_parse_json would still attempt to JSON-decode it, leaving the corruption bug unfixed for that common case. 2032 does cover a broader set of unions (str|int, str|float, str|bool) that 3056 doesn't address, but it misses the Annotated case that's central to the reported bug.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395's fix is per-request: it targets the specific pending JSON-RPC call via read_stream_writer and explicitly checks `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which expect no reply) aren't mishandled, plus it upgrades the log line from debug to warning for better observability of exhausted retries. #3098's diff includes an unrelated revert of `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` back to `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of the file, which is a stale-branch/rebase artifact and a likely source of merge conflicts against current main; its exception-based approach also surfaces failure at the connection/exception-group level rather than resolving the specific in-flight request that was waiting.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the StreamableHTTP client exhausts its SSE reconnection attempts after a server disconnect, the failure is currently swallowed silently (only a debug log), leaving the in-flight request's caller hanging forever with no response or exception. Both PRs target exactly this 'reconnection failure' path in `_handle_reconnection`/its callers, just via different signaling mechanisms: #2395 constructs a `JSONRPCError` and sends it through `ctx.read_stream_writer` so the specific pending request resolves with an error (skipping notifications via an `isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest)` guard), while #3098 instead raises a `StreamableHTTPError`, adding an `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull it out of anyio's `ExceptionGroup` wrapping so it propagates to the caller as a Python exception. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both add near-identical quote/escape-aware comma splitters (compare the char-by-char loops in _iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041 - same logic, same edge cases handled for backslash escapes inside quotes). The functional difference: #3012's _iter_www_auth_params finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which assumes the header contains a single challenge/scheme. #3041 goes further with _extract_bearer_auth_params, which partitions each top-level segment into scheme/remainder and explicitly scopes extraction to segments belonging to the 'Bearer' scheme, so it degrades correctly instead of merging params from a second scheme (e.g. a trailing DPoP challenge) into the Bearer result. This makes #3041 the more complete fix for headers with multiple concatenated challenges.

clusters.pick_reason: 3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() before checking the union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP pattern Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None. 2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` directly against the raw union args without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated-wrapped str member (very common when params carry a Field description) is not recognized as 'simple' and pre_parse_json would still attempt to JSON-decode it, leaving the corruption bug unfixed for that common case. 2032 does cover a broader set of unions (str|int, str|float, str|bool) that 3056 doesn't address, but it misses the Annotated case that's central to the reported bug.

members.cluster_pick_reason: 3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() before checking the union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP pattern Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None. 2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` directly against the raw union args without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated-wrapped str member (very common when params carry a Field description) is not recognized as 'simple' and pre_parse_json would still attempt to JSON-decode it, leaving the corruption bug unfixed for that common case. 2032 does cover a broader set of unions (str|int, str|float, str|bool) that 3056 doesn't address, but it misses the Annotated case that's central to the reported bug.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395's fix is per-request: it targets the specific pending JSON-RPC call via read_stream_writer and explicitly checks `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which expect no reply) aren't mishandled, plus it upgrades the log line from debug to warning for better observability of exhausted retries. #3098's diff includes an unrelated revert of `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` back to `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of the file, which is a stale-branch/rebase artifact and a likely source of merge conflicts against current main; its exception-based approach also surfaces failure at the connection/exception-group level rather than resolving the specific in-flight request that was waiting.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the StreamableHTTP client exhausts its SSE reconnection attempts after a server disconnect, the failure is currently swallowed silently (only a debug log), leaving the in-flight request's caller hanging forever with no response or exception. Both PRs target exactly this 'reconnection failure' path in `_handle_reconnection`/its callers, just via different signaling mechanisms: #2395 constructs a `JSONRPCError` and sends it through `ctx.read_stream_writer` so the specific pending request resolves with an error (skipping notifications via an `isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest)` guard), while #3098 instead raises a `StreamableHTTPError`, adding an `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull it out of anyio's `ExceptionGroup` wrapping so it propagates to the caller as a Python exception. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #3263 fixes cold-start refresh by rediscovering AS metadata with an added issuer-binding check, which validates the resolved endpoint before use and guards against acting on stale/mismatched metadata — a check #2492 lacks since it persists and reuses metadata from storage without re-validation. #3263 also avoids widening the public TokenStorage protocol (#2492 adds two new get/set_oauth_metadata methods every storage backend implementation must consider), and coordinates with the existing eager-discovery path via the new eager_discovery_attempted flag to avoid re-probing metadata-less servers on every refresh.

clusters.pick_reason: #2962's test explicitly cites SEP-1577, which states tool_result blocks MUST be preceded by tool_use, but there is no requirement that a tool_use MUST be followed by a tool_result — so relaxing the check (not raising) matches the actual protocol spec. #3053 does the opposite: it raises a new ValueError enforcing that every tool_use have a matching tool_result, which contradicts SEP-1577 as cited in #2962, and its diff omits any spec justification for the added constraint.

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs touch the exact same conditional in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) governing what happens when a previous tool_use has no matching tool_result in the current message — the same underlying case reported in issue #2960. However, they resolve it with opposite behavior: #2962 guards the id-matching check with has_tool_results so that a tool_use with no following tool_result is silently allowed (no raise); #3053 instead adds an explicit raise ValueError(...) for that exact case, enforcing the opposite requirement. clusters.pick_reason: Both add near-identical quote/escape-aware comma splitters (compare the char-by-char loops in _iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041 - same logic, same edge cases handled for backslash escapes inside quotes). The functional difference: #3012's _iter_www_auth_params finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which assumes the header contains a single challenge/scheme. #3041 goes further with _extract_bearer_auth_params, which partitions each top-level segment into scheme/remainder and explicitly scopes extraction to segments belonging to the 'Bearer' scheme, so it degrades correctly instead of merging params from a second scheme (e.g. a trailing DPoP challenge) into the Bearer result. This makes #3041 the more complete fix for headers with multiple concatenated challenges.
